chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, from Al-Fudayl, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'We invite the people to this matter (Wilayah/Imamate).' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'O Fudayl! Indeed, when Allah intends good for a servant, He commands an angel, who seizes him by his neck until He brings him into this matter, willingly or unwillingly.'

key_terms.الْأَمْرِ: The matter (referring to Wilayah or Imamate)

ai.seo_question: How does Allah ensure a person enters the station of Wilayah?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the call to Wilayah is not merely a human invitation but a divine compulsion (*al-amr al-ilahi*), where Allah Himself seizes the servant by the neck to ensure entry into the station of Imamate. This highlights the Shia concept of *al-amr al-ilahi* (divine command) as an active, forceful bestowal of grace that overrides human hesitation, distinguishing it from mere intellectual persuasion. The phrase 'willingly or unwillingly' (*ta'i'an aw karihan*) underscores the inevitability of this spiritual reality for those chosen by God.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Marwan, from Al Fuzayl who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘We tend to invite the people to this matter (Al-Wilayah)’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Fuzayl! Whenever Allah Intends goodness with a servant, Commands an Angels, so he seizes him by his neck until he enter him into this matter (Al-Wilayah), willingly or unwillingly’.
en.sarwar: 3. Abu Ali al-Ash’ari has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Marwan from al-Fudayl who has said the following:

“Once I said to abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) ‘Should we invite people to this cause (belief of Shi’a Muslims)?’ The Imam said, ‘O al-Fudayl, it is certain, when Allah wills good for a servant. He commands an angel who holds his neck until he brings him into this cause whether he likes or dislikes it.’”
